gen-dafont-starborn-gf-pt-sans-caption: Dreamy letters drift apart across Starborn, each line a thick dark stripe. PT Sans Caption can stay at a modest size, since its big-bodied lowercase and bowls left inviting and unclosed fill the line well.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-puritan: Puritan is all rounded forms, open to the side and friendly. Starborn is at its best drifting through wide gaps in a dark, dreamy headline, while the sans body is best at big, open e and a counters.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-questrial: Starborn spaces its letters far apart, then packs each lowercase line into a thick, dark stripe. But Questrial does its best work in plain-spoken r, n and m shapes whose arches match their stems.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada reads full and tall, every curve open at its end. Starborn does its best with dreamy display lettering and wide gaps, while Radio Canada is best at steady, single-weight sans-serif lines.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big keeps a monoline skeleton, its terminals finishing well away from the stem. Radio Canada Big's tall x-height fills the line, while Starborn drifts dreamily in wide-spaced, dark stripes.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-readex-pro: Starborn scatters its letters across wide gaps of blank space, each lowercase line a thick, dark stripe. Starborn dreams up top; Readex Pro stays steady below, broad-gapped and hairline-free.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-roboto: Wide stretches of blank space between letters give Starborn a dreamy, thick-striped look, with every line of lowercase running dark. Roboto, a plain sans, keeps its round letters generously open.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-ruda: Ethereal and dreamy, Starborn spaces its letters far apart and sets each line as a thick, dark stripe. Ruda, a plain sans, adds a sizable x-height plus a wire-like skeleton.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-saira: Starborn drifts, wide-spaced and dreamy, in thick dark stripes. Saira, a plain sans, then steps in with rounded letters stretching high and a see-through gap in every s, so the dreamy heading meets tidy text.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch keeps a compact gap between x-height and ascender line, with a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e. Starborn dreams in wide gaps; Sarpanch, a plain sans, keeps things compact.
